page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v7 is an entry-tier virtual machine within the memory-optimized Esv7 series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 execution threads on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, configured with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large shared 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-Tile, alongside hardware cryptography extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio aligned with memory-optimized profiles. It lacks bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external Azure managed disks for operating system and data persistence. Measured uncached memory throughput reflects entry-level dual-thread limits, reaching 22.5 GB/sec for large-block sequential reads and 11.72 GB/sec for sequential writes, alongside 167.98 GB/sec in small-block cached operations.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-threaded capability. Single-core Geekbench reached 2222.0 and text processing scored 2538.0, both placing in the upper quartile. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 35.12 GB/sec. Conversely, overall throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU allocation: multi-core Geekbench registered 2827.0, PassMark CPU reached 4226.65, and multi-core stress-ng placed in the lower decile at 2201.38. Database operations and Redis throughput achieved modest tiers at 1257.19 and 3.99 million operations per second respectively.

Given its high memory allocation relative to compute cores, the E2s_v7 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute. Primary use cases include lightweight in-memory caching tiers, small enterprise relational databases, staging environments, low-traffic web backends, and text-oriented batch ingestion tasks.
